title: Connect checkout handoff and verify pending-order runtime
verify: The authenticated checkout continuation submits a cart reference and fresh idempotency key to pending-order creation after FT-006 validation.
The storefront renders a truthful pending-order handoff with order ID and expiry without claiming payment success or calling a provider.
Real browser/backend evidence proves one order and reservation set, same-order retry, stock-conflict no-mutation, controlled expiry, released reservations, and cleanup.
No client-calculated tariff, line item, customer ID, or payment-provider result becomes authoritative.
Artifacts contain no PII, credentials, cookies, tokens, production data, or provider payloads.
T3 verification records semantic-pass, HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done, and ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_NOTE: present.
evidence_required: Browser report proving authenticated checkout-to-pending-order handoff and no provider request.
Backend report proving order/reservation counts, duplicate retry identity, stock conflict compensation, expiry, and cleanup.
Privacy scan, released ports/processes, typecheck/build/lint output, and full T3 closure markers.
constraints: Keep the FT-004 authenticated_ready gate and existing FT-006 validation boundary.
Do not add payment-provider calls, webhook behavior, order Admin replacement, or direct database browser access.
Publish evidence only after synthetic fixtures, processes, and ports are cleaned up.
Use runtime assertions rather than report-only success flags.
invariants: Only authenticated customers can create pending orders.
A retry cannot silently create a second order or reservation set.
The browser never marks payment successful.
Expired pending orders have no active reservation items after cleanup.
purpose: Prove that the real authenticated checkout flow hands off to one truthful pending order and reservation lifecycle.
success_outcome: A sanitized real browser/backend run demonstrates pending order creation, retry safety, expiry release, and provider isolation across the complete FT-007 boundary.
anti_goals: Do not implement or verify FT-009 payment provider behavior.
Do not implement complete FT-008 order lifecycle/Admin visibility.
Do not use fake server, direct database browser access, production data, or hardcoded success reports.

forbidden_scope: FT-009 payment-provider calls, webhook, or credentials
production data, secrets, direct browser database access
stop_conditions: The real authenticated browser/backend boundary cannot be exercised.
Evidence cannot prove no provider request and no duplicate order/reservation.
Cleanup or privacy guarantees cannot be made reproducible.
The handoff requires changing FT-004 auth or FT-006 parser/validation decisions.
